Order 
This petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India has been filed assailing the order dated 16/10/2024 passed by respondent No.4, whereby Second Appeal preferred by the petitioner has been rejected.

2 . It is the case of the petitioner that the petitioner is having Constitutional right to seek the Income Tax Return under the Right to Information Act and produce it in the matrimonial case so that the truth can be shown before the Court as a matrimonial case between the petitioner and Dr. Deepali Sahu is pending in the High Court and before the various Courts.
It is argued that Dr. Deepali Sahu has been filing Income Tax Returns with the Income Tax Department since year 2013, but she conceals her income and claims she has no independent income.
Dr. Deepali Sahu maintains 15 bank accounts.
She runs her own independent clinic and serves as a duty Doctor in various hospitals.

She has joint accounts with her parents and NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:502 2 WP-5821-2025 brother, which contain transactions of more than Lakhs of Rupees.
Dr. Deepali Sahu's family operates a clothing business in which she is a partner.
3 . It is argued by learned counsel for the petitioner that Dr. Deepali Sahu requested the petitioner's Income Tax Return which was provided to her by the Income Tax Commissioner's Office.

Petitioner also submitted an application dated 26/03/2023 under the Right to Information Act to the Public Information Officer in the Income Tax Commissioner's office seeking information on 10 points.

In the said application, Income Tax Returns of Dr. Deepali Sahu, Mr. Jairam Sahu, Mrs. Durgesh Sahu,

sentences.text: Mr. Dipanshu Sahu, and Mrs. Vandana Sahu were sought, as this information was required to be submitted in a matrimonial case.
Thereafter, information regarding points 1 to 4 was given and information regarding points 5 to 10 was not given.
Being aggrieved by the aforesaid, petitioner filed First Appeal, which was dismissed on 10.05.2023.

Against which, petitioner filed a Second Appeal,
hearing whereof was held online on 14.10.2024.

During the hearing, the competent Authority verbally stated that an order would be passed to provide the information, but on 16.10.2024,
petitioner's second appeal was dismissed vide order impugned.

It is argued that Dr. Deepali Sahu has been continuously concealing the facts of her income, therefore, it is necessary that the Income Tax Returns of her along with her family should be called from the Income Tax Department so that the lies told by Dr. Deepali Sahu can be proved before the Court so that the cases can be resolved.
It is further argued that the respondents are deliberately withholding information under the Right to Information Act from the petitioner.

The petitioner is facing NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:502 3 WP-5821-2025 charges under Section 125 of Cr.P.C, under Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act and under Section 498A of IPC.
Therefore, it is prayed that the respondents be directed to provide the petitioner all the desired information.

4 . On notice being issued, reply has been filed by the respondents, wherein it is categorically stated that the contention regarding information with respect to Dr. Deepali Sahu has been denied to the petitioner, is incorrect because petitioner has not furnished the complete details in the application like the PAN Card details of Dr. Deepali Sahu to enable the Authorities to ascertain the documents demanded by the petitioner.
The petitioner was requested to provide PAN number of Dr. Deepali Sahu, but he has not furnished the same.

The ground raised by the petitioner that details of the petitioner were furnished to Dr. Deepali Sahu under RTI Act but the same has been denied to the petitioner, is also denied on the ground that Dr. Deepali Sahu has furnished complete details in the RTI application.
Therefore, the said documents could be supplied to her.
It is only the net and gross taxable income details which are provided to Dr. Deepali Sahu with respect to the petitioner, but no copy of the ITR was supplied.
If the petitioner furnishes the detail particulars of PAN card as required by the Department, they will surely provide the detail particulars as asked by the petitioner under the RTI application.
The rejection order clearly demonstrate the aforesaid aspect.

Therefore,
they have prayed for dismissal of the Writ Petition.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

The reason which is reflected from the rejection order is as under:-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:502 4 WP-5821-2025 "6. 6-8 PANs of the persons mentioned are not ascertainable in order to send the application to respective CPIOs.
In case PAN is ascertained, the application may be submitted to the respective CPIOs.
7. 9-10 Jurisdiction of the assessee vests with the ITO- Ward-1(1), Jabalpur.

You are requested to submit application to the office of the ITO-Ward-1(1),
Jabalpur."

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid, there is no illegality in passing the order impugned.

However, the fact remains that the Authorities themselves have mentioned in reply to paragraph 6.1 that if a fresh application is filed providing the complete details, the required information will be supplied to the petitioner.

8. Under these circumstances, this petition is disposed of directing the petitioner to file a fresh application under the Right to Information Act providing all the detail particulars including the PAN number to enable the respondents to process the application and supply the desired information to him.

If such an application is filed within a period of 15 days from today, the Authorities are directed to dwell upon the same and supply the necessary information to the petitioner within a period of 30 days thereafter.
9. With aforesaid observations, the petition is finally disposed of.
No order as to costs.

(VISHAL MISHRA) JUDGE Shbhnkr Dr. Lalit Chaturvedi vs Aaykar Ayukt on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148197042/
